## Overview

**Aegon, The Rogue Paragon** — a human paladin of **Aurelius**, god of wisdom and justice. One of the strongest and most divinely touched members of his order, yet he has defied their commands and follows his own ideals. A paradox: faithful yet rebellious, honoured yet hunted by the shadows of a truth he does not yet know.

---

## Appearance

A tall, broad-shouldered human with the build of a veteran warrior. Wears the armour of the Order of the Protectors — though it shows field modifications, personal touches marking a man who follows his own path. Face weathered, eyes carrying hard-won wisdom. A holy symbol of Aurelius hangs at his neck. At his side: a warhammer.

---

## Background

### Origins
Aegon's mother died in childbirth. His father abandoned them before Aegon was born — no name, no reason. A local maester brought the infant to a chapel known to accept orphans. The priest who welcomed him was named **Paul**.

### Father Paul
Paul was a gentleman in his forties — kind, wise, intelligent, deeply religious. But he was not an ordinary priest. He could detect truth from lies, was skilled in combat, and carried himself with warrior discipline. Paul belonged to a knightly sub-order within the **Order of the Scales** called **the Order of the Protectors** — paladins and warriors who followed Aurelius, took oaths to protect the innocent, and swore to defeat evil.

Paul raised Aegon as his own son. Aegon showed remarkable talent with weapons. But more impressive were his emerging powers: healing with a touch, instinctive magic detection, and **visions** — fragments of past, present, and future that came to him in dreams. Paul recognized these signs. Aegon was a **Paragon** — a paladin with an extraordinary connection to Aurelius, seemingly receiving more divine favour than any other.

### The Order of the Protectors
An independent knightly chapter **within** the broader Order of the Scales:
- **Order of the Scales** (main church of Aurelius) provides monetary support, requests missions
- **Order of the Protectors** answers calls but maintains its own hierarchy and traditions
- Both share the **High Septon** — central temple of Aurelius in the old capital of Kythoria

The Protectors' warriors are taken to the High Septon and trained from a young age in combat, war, history, and religion. After three years of tests and trials, they swear an oath before Aurelius and choose a holy symbol. With the oath made, they leave to travel the world, obeying the High Council and honouring their god.

> **Oath of the Order:** *"Do not fear your enemies. Be courageous and upright so that Aurelius may love you. Always speak the truth, even if it leads to your death. Safeguard the defenceless and stop evil in this world. This is your oath."*

Aegon chose to join. He knelt before the statues of Aurelius, swore the oath, and chose his holy symbol: his **warhammer**.

### The Rogue Paragon
For years, Aegon served faithfully — completing missions, growing in power. His status as a Paragon became known. The High Council watched him with interest. Some whispered he was destined to lead. Others grew jealous — fanatics who believed drinking his blood might bring them closer to Aurelius, or traditionalists who saw his unique nature as a threat to the Order's hierarchy.

Then came the news: Paul's chapel had been attacked. Aegon rode immediately. He found Paul on the chapel floor, covered in wounds. Aegon reached for his healing powers, but Paul stopped him. With his last strength, he whispered:

> *"Do not trust the Order... Trust your oath and your visions..."*

And Paul died.

An investigation was announced. Weeks passed. Months. No answers. No culprit named. The matter faded from official attention.

Aegon did not push for answers — not because he was satisfied, but because Paul's dying words consumed him. *"Do not trust the Order... Trust your oath and your visions."* He began to watch the Order more closely. He started questioning commands that felt wrong. Sometimes he refused orders outright when his visions or oath demanded otherwise.

The High Council grew frustrated. Some called him heretic. Others whispered his Paragon status made him uncontrollable. But they could not expel him — he was too powerful, too visibly favoured by Aurelius.

And within Aegon, something else was changing. His visions began to shift. Where once Aurelius's voice was clear, a new whisper grew in its place. Older. Stranger. Pulling him toward a truth the Order did not want him to find.

The title came from both allies and enemies: **Aegon, The Rogue Paragon** — a paladin who could not be commanded, only trusted to follow his own path.

---

## Abilities
- **Paladin's Power:** Divine smite, lay on hands, aura of protection — channelled through his oath to Aurelius
- **Paragon's Blessing:** Unusually strong connection to the Weave, interpreted by the Order as divine favour
- **Visions:** Dreams of past, present, and future — initially from Aurelius, now shifting toward B's consciousness
- **Exceptional Combatant:** Master of warhammers, swords, spears, and axes
- **Independent Will:** Resistant to coercion, manipulation, and blind obedience

---

## Goals
1. Understand why Paul warned him against the Order — what did his dying words mean?
2. Understand why his visions are changing and where they truly come from
3. Uphold his oath — protect the innocent, defeat evil — even if it means defying the Order
4. Navigate growing hostility from those within the Order who fear or covet his power

---

## Relationships
- **Paul (deceased)** — Father figure, mentor. Aegon has not investigated Paul's death — consumed by the question of *why* Paul warned him.
- **The Order of the Scales** — Parent organization. Aegon still serves but no longer follows blindly.
- **The Order of the Protectors** — His knightly chapter. Some support his independence; others see defiance.
- **Aurelius** — The god he swore his oath to. Remains faithful, but shifting visions raise questions.
- **The Crimson Covenant** — Organization Aegon knows little about. Investigation into Paul's death produced no named culprits.

## Open Questions
1. [?] **Who was Aegon's biological father?** Mother died in childbirth, father disappeared before Aegon was born — no name, no trace. Could be deliberate erasure connected to wider conspiracy.
2. [?] **What exactly did Paul know?** His dying words suggest he discovered something about the Order.
3. [?] **Who attacked Paul's chapel?** Investigation produced no results. (GM note: evidence planted by Order frames the Crimson Covenant.)
4. [?] **The jealous/fanatic members** — How far will they go to claim Aegon's power?
5. [?] **The old capital** — The High Septon is there. What other secrets does it hold?
6. [?] **B's influence on Aegon** — Will his visions grow clear enough to reveal the truth about the Originals and the gods' deception?
